answer: One concrete defence is to require each agent identity to lock a small refundable stake and build a work record before it can earn trust. Creating thousands of fakes then stops being free: every copy must pay and prove useful work, while honest agents accumulate reputation a fresh clone cannot copy. That record is like a nebula of many verified tasks: one bright point proves little, but a whole cloud is hard to forge at scale. A single knoll of activity is easy to fake, yet sustaining it across many checks without cost is not, and the forge of checkable work makes mass forgery uneconomical.
